label: e1a-artmerge-10y
_why: THE e1-ANCHOR BOOK, PROBED (user-ruled 2026-10-01, BALANCE_FRAMEWORK 10.91.5, FINDINGS F197: 'Agreed on e1/1.5 instead of e1/A; e1/B, engines, the 60% and pop-good penalty' ... 'go: probes and then runs'). Book config/mod_config.e1a-artmerge.json = the arm at the ruled 2-pound craft floor (artmerge6-pb-f2) with every industry anchored at e1 (e2 xA, e3 xA^2, cost following the anchor), the step down to e0 /1.5 on output and input value, motor on [1,2,3], the pop-good industries' anchor-and-below input lift 1.4, the 60% craft rule (0.6 of vanilla's goods per worker, the floor crossed at 0.89 of base) and the output-matched 1836 craft seeding (3,441 craft levels in 60 countries, 6.88M people typed from peasants, head count unchanged). Two seeds 1836 -> 1846 on F191's instrument plus a 1837.12.1 dump for F149's chain readings.

_questions.Q1: Health against the canon's six runs at 1846 (health_vs_ref.mjs): no dead industry, no token market.
_questions.Q2: The 1836 supply anchor: production of the craft goods and of steel, engines, tools at 1836.2.1 in the instrumented markets against vanilla's (the n=16 baseline's 1836.2.1 dumps).
_questions.Q3: The chain at 1837.12.1 (F149): steel and engines - production and the share of price readings at the +75% ceiling - against the canon and vanilla.
_questions.Q4: The crafts at 1846: staffed levels, value added per worker-year against the 2-pound floor, failed hires (hiring_census.mjs / craft_fill.mjs on the kept saves), and whether the seeded crafts keep their staff.
_questions.Q5: World GDP at 1846 against the canon's six and the 2-pound arm (20261001_115032); 1836 urban centres against the canon (the build's +69 estimate).
_questions.Q6: Motor: steam-engine levels built 1836-1846 (its ai_value is now 3,000 as an e1 rung) and the engine price path against the canon.

_predictions.Q1: no dead industry; the craft goods' cells nearer the canon's than the arm's (more craft output at the start)
_predictions.Q2: craft goods' 1836.2.1 production within +-15% of vanilla's (the crafts now make vanilla's e0 output; the e1 blocks make exactly vanilla's) - the arm's was well under; steel 0.9-1.1 of vanilla (its e0 at 0.92 of vanilla's output, margin kept); tools still over vanilla's (tooling's e2 blocks at 1.65x)
_predictions.Q3: steel at the ceiling in no more of the readings than the canon's 18%; engines production at or above the canon's (the steam rung's AI desire tripled)
_predictions.Q4: crafts staffed 85-98% at 1846 like F191; value added per worker-year 3-7 pounds in 1840-1846 (prices above base early), above the floor
_predictions.Q5: world GDP within -5% / +3% of the canon's at 1846 (weaker e1 rungs in food, paper, steel, explosives against more craft output); urban centres +10-15% at 1836.2.1
_predictions.Q6: more motor levels by 1846 than the canon (1,000 -> 3,000 desire); engines cheaper by 1840-1845

_cost: 2 runs x 1836 -> 1846, about 13 minutes each plus builds and harvest
_caveats: Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30).
Ten years speak to the anchor and the early game only; obsolescence is the century's question (a 2+1 follows if this reads healthy).
Two seeds: a probe, no register reading. No stop watcher.
